recipe.name: Grilled Lamb Kofta with Charred Vegetables and Tahini
instructions: In a bowl, combine ground lamb, grated onion, parsley, cumin, cinnamon, garlic and salt; mix well and shape into 4 oblong kofta.
Toss zucchini, red bell pepper and cauliflower with olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to high heat.
Grill the kofta for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Grill the vegetables alongside, turning occasionally, until tender and charred in spots, about 8-10 minutes.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice and water until smooth to make the sauce.
Plate the kofta with the grilled vegetables, drizzle with tahini sauce and sprinkle with sumac.
recipe.prep_notes: Yields 4 portions, eaten across 1 day(s). Portion immediately, refrigerate in airtight containers; reheat thoroughly before serving.

recipe.name: Grilled Chicken and Hummus Wrap
instructions: Season chicken with cumin, paprika, salt and pepper; grill or pan-sear until cooked through, then slice.
Warm the tortilla briefly on a dry skillet to soften.
Spread hummus and greek yogurt over the tortilla.
Layer lettuce, tomato, cucumber, red onion, feta and sliced chicken.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice.
Roll tightly into a wrap, slice in half and serve.

recipe.name: Mediterranean Roast Pork Loin with Lemon Potatoes, Roasted Peppers and Fennel
instructions: Preheat oven to 210°C (fan).
Toss potato wedges, fennel, red pepper and red onion with half the olive oil, half the garlic, oregano, salt and pepper on a roasting tray.
Roast vegetables for 15 minutes while preparing the pork.
Rub pork loin with remaining olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Push vegetables to one side of the tray, place pork loin in the center and roast together for 30-35 minutes until pork reaches 63°C internal temperature and vegetables are golden and tender.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then slice.
Scatter kalamata olives over the vegetables and serve alongside the sliced pork with pan juices.
recipe.prep_notes: Yields 4 portions, eaten across 1 day(s). Portion immediately, refrigerate in airtight containers; reheat thoroughly before serving.

recipe.name: Korean Beef Bulgogi Rice Tray Bake
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C.
Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, honey and gochujang into a marinade.
Toss sliced beef in half the marinade and let sit 10 minutes.
Spread rice across a lined baking tray, top with sliced zucchini and carrot.
Arrange marinated beef over the vegetables and drizzle remaining marinade evenly.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until beef is cooked and vegetables are tender.
Fry the egg separately to a runny yolk and place on top before serving.
Garnish with spring onion and sesame seeds.
recipe.prep_notes: Yields 4 portions, eaten across 1 day(s). Portion immediately, refrigerate in airtight containers; reheat thoroughly before serving.

recipe.name: Pan-Seared Lemon-Spiced Chicken with Kidney Bean & Savoy Cabbage Skillet
instructions: Toss chicken breasts with lemon juice, lemon zest, paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and sear for 5-7 minutes per side until cooked through, then remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the shredded Savoy cabbage and kidney beans. Sauté for 4-5 minutes until the cabbage is tender-crisp.
Slice the chicken, return it to the skillet to warm through, and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.

recipe.name: Oven-Braised Aussie Mince Chow Mein with Edamame Noodles
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (140°C fan-forced). Prepare a heavy-based casserole dish or Dutch oven that has a tight-fitting lid.

Place the casserole dish on the stovetop over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Add the beef mince, breaking it up into fine pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook until browned. Lower the heat slightly, then toss in the diced onion, garlic, and ginger. Sauté for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant, stirring well to combine with the beef.

Stir the grated green apple, finely diced carrots, and celery into the beef mixture. In a small jug, whisk together the beef broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and curry powder. Pour this over the ingredients and stir everything together well. Bring it to a gentle simmer. Cover tightly with the lid and transfer the dish to the preheated oven. Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

While the mince is in its final minutes in the oven, bring a separate pot of salted water to the boil. Cook the edamame pasta for 3 to 5 minutes until al dente. Drain, rinse briefly with warm water, and set aside. Carefully remove the casserole dish from the oven and lift the lid. Stir the shredded cabbage into the hot mince mixture. Replace the lid and return it to the oven for a final 15 minutes, just until the cabbage is tender. Remove from the oven, toss in the cooked edamame noodles and sliced green onions, and stir gently until the noodles are completely coated. Serve hot.

recipe.name: Keto Broccoli Buns
instructions: In a bowl, combine the almond flour, salt, dried garlic, coconut flour, psyllium husk, and baking powder.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs, then mix in the Greek yogurt and 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Add the shredded mozzarella and finely chopped green onions to the egg mixture and mix well.
Finely chop the broccoli head with stems removed.
Heat olive oil in a frypan, add the broccoli and a splash of water, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Puree the cooked broccoli lightly with an immersion blender, then add it to the bowl with the wet ingredients.
Add the dry ingredient mixture into the wet ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Grease your hands and shape the dough into buns.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the buns and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 22 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown.

recipe.name: Ginger Chicken Soup with Sweet Potato Noodles
instructions: Heat the garlic-infused olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the sliced ginger and lemongrass, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the chicken thighs and sear for 2 minutes on each side to build a bit of color.
Pour in the chicken bone broth and bring to a boil. Turn the heat down to low, cover with a lid, and let it gently simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and completely cooked through.

While the soup simmers, bring a separate pot of water to a boil. Cook the sweet potato glass noodles for 6 to 7 minutes until they are translucent and chewy. Drain, rinse under cold water to stop the cooking, and set aside.

Remove the chicken thighs from the broth and shred them using two forks. Drop the sliced carrots into the simmering broth for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then add the bok choy or spinach and the shredded chicken back into the pot for the final 60 seconds to wilt the greens.

Turn off the heat. Stir in the tamari, sesame oil, and the chopped spring onion greens. Divide the cooked sweet potato noodles into serving bowls and ladle the piping hot chicken ginger broth and vegetables directly over them. Top with fresh coriander.

recipe.name: Blueberry Pancakes with Orange-Almond Butter
instructions: Prepare the Orange-Almond Butter: Microwave 2 tablespoons of butter in a medium bowl until melted, about 1 minute. Stir in 2 teaspoons orange zest, 2 teaspoons honey, 1/4 teaspoon almond extract, 1/8 teaspoon salt, and the remaining 6 tablespoons of butter. Let mixture stand for 2 minutes, then whisk until smooth.
Prepare the Pancake Batter: Whisk 70g all-purpose flour, 100g wholemeal self-raising flour, 30g oats, 2 tablespoons sugar, 12g baking powder, 2g baking soda, and 2.5g salt together in a large bowl.
Whisk 2 eggs and 45g oil in a second medium bowl until well combined. Whisk 270g milk and 7g vanilla paste into the egg mixture.
Add the egg mixture to the flour mixture and stir gently until just combined (batter should remain lumpy with a few streaks of flour). Let batter sit for 10 minutes before cooking.

Cook the Pancakes: Heat 1/2 teaspoon oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat to 190°C until shimmering. Using paper towels, carefully wipe out oil, leaving a thin film on the bottom and sides of the skillet.
Drop 1 tablespoon batter in the center of the skillet. If the test pancake is pale golden brown after 1 minute, the skillet is ready.
Portion batter into the skillet in 3 places using a 1/4-cup measure, leaving 2 inches between portions. Gently spread batter into 4-inch rounds if necessary.
Cook until edges are set, first sides are golden brown, and bubbles on surface begin to break (2 to 3 minutes). Gently fold in or scatter blueberries as desired while cooking.
Flip pancakes using a thin spatula and cook second sides until golden brown (1 to 2 minutes longer).
Repeat with remaining batter and remaining oil as necessary. Serve warm topped with Orange-Almond Butter.

recipe.name: Korean Air Fryer Chicken
instructions: Line the air fryer basket with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, vinegar, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, ginger, salt, and pepper and toss to coat the chicken. Let marinate for 15 to 20 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl.
Put the cornstarch in a separate shallow bowl.
Dunk the chicken pieces first in the egg and then in the cornstarch to coat. Arrange the coated chicken pieces on the parchment paper in the air fryer.
Once all of the chicken is coated and arranged in the air fryer (you will likely have to do this in 2 batches), spritz or brush the chicken with a bit of cooking oil.
Air fry the chicken at 400ºF for 8 minutes. Turn the chicken pieces over, spritz or brush with a bit more oil, and then cook for another 7 minutes at 400ºF.
While the chicken is cooking, make the sauce. In a small bowl, stir together the ketchup, gochujang paste, honey, remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic until well combined.
When the chicken is finished air frying, transfer it to a medium bowl and toss with the sauce. Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.

recipe.name: Fifty-Fifty Bolognese
instructions: Heat a large, heavy-based saucepan or casserole over low-medium heat, add 1/2 cup of olive oil, onion and garlic and fry for about 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and fry for a further 8 minutes, stirring regularly until softened and lightly browned.
Add the mince and fry for 3 minutes until it begins to brown, then add the wine, passata, salt, oregano, tomato sauce and 1 cup of water, stirring to scrape up any fond from the base of the pot.
Cover, reduce to a low heat and simmer for 1 hour, stirring once or twice.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add salt. Add the spaghetti and boil for one minute less than the packet directions, or until al dente.
Remove the spaghetti from the pot and add it directly to the bolognese sauce with an extra 2 tablespoons of olive oil and about 2 tablespoons of the pasta water.
Stir well over medium heat for about 1 minute to combine the pasta and sauce.
Serve immediately with the finely shredded parsley and freshly grated parmesan cheese.

recipe.name: Slow Cooked Beef Cheeks
instructions: Trim any large fatty membranes off the beef cheeks. Pat dry, then season all over with 1 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over high heat. Sear the beef cheeks in batches until nicely browned on all sides, then transfer to a plate.
Turn heat down to medium-high and heat the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil. Add the minced garlic and diced onion, sautéing for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the diced celery and carrot, sautéing for another 3 minutes.
Transfer the sautéed vegetables to a slow cooker and place the browned beef cheeks on top.
Pour the red wine into the pot over high heat, bring to a simmer for 1 minute while scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Pour the warm wine into the slow cooker along with the beef stock, thyme, bay leaves, remaining salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 to 10 hours (or High for 6 to 8 hours) until the beef cheeks are tender.
Remove beef cheeks from the slow cooker and discard the thyme stems and bay leaves.
Blend the braising liquid with an immersion blender until smooth.
Transfer the sauce to a saucepan and simmer over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes until reduced by 1/4 to 1/3 into a rich gravy consistency.
Return the beef cheeks to the sauce and adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipe.name: Chocolate Broccoli & Berry Bio-Activator Smoothie
instructions: Pour low-fat kefir and liquid egg whites into high-speed blender container.
Add frozen broccoli florets, frozen mixed berries, rolled oats, chia seeds, mustard seed powder, and Ceylon cinnamon.
Top with chocolate protein powder and creatine monohydrate.
Blend on high speed for 60 seconds until smooth, creamy, and homogenized.
recipe.prep_notes: Combine liquids first to ensure smooth blending. Blend on high power for 60 seconds to break down raw oats and frozen broccoli.

recipe.name: Seed Bread with Egg Cheese Topping
instructions: Grind half of the flaxseeds and leave the other half whole.
Pan toast the pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, and sesame seeds until warm and lightly fragrant.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground almond, psyllium, flaxseeds, baking powder, salt, and the toasted seeds.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 3 eggs, yogurt, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil.
Combine the egg mixture with the dry ingredients and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Line a bread pan with parchment paper and oil lightly. Pour the mixture into the pan and shape it.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 45 to 55 minutes until firm and fully cooked.
To prepare the topping: mix soft cheese, chopped boiled eggs, chopped spring onions, chopped fresh basil, salt, black pepper, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and chopped sun-dried tomatoes in a bowl.
Slice the baked bread and spread the egg and herb cheese topping on top.
recipe.prep_notes: Store bread in an airtight container or slice and freeze. Prepare topping fresh or keep refrigerated for up to 3 days.

recipe.name: Salmon Meal Prep with Cilantro-Lime Rice and Broccoli
instructions: Rinse the white rice and cook in an Instant Pot or saucepan with water and a pinch of salt until fluffy.
Fluff cooked rice with a fork and stir in the butter, fresh lime juice, and chopped cilantro.
Season salmon fillets with salt and drizzle with olive oil. Pan-sear in a skillet over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Steam broccoli florets until tender-crisp and season lightly with salt.
Warm dinner rolls in the oven if desired.
Divide salmon, cilantro-lime rice, steamed broccoli, and dinner rolls equally into meal-prep containers or freezer-safe trays.

recipe.name: Chipotle Loaded Bean Salad
instructions: To make Dressing #1, combine the extra virgin olive oil, olive oil mayonnaise, chipotle pepper, adobo sauce, garlic clove, tomato sauce, yellow mustard, apple cider vinegar, and ground cumin in a small blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas, kidney beans, cannellini beans, and black beans thoroughly.

In a large salad bowl, combine all four drained beans, diced capsicum, shredded carrot, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced olives, shredded red cabbage, finely diced red onion, sliced spring onion, and corn kernels.
Add chopped parsley and coriander to the bowl.
Pour Dressing #1 over the bean and vegetable mixture.
Toss well until all ingredients are evenly coated in the dressing. Serve fresh or chill before serving.

recipe.name: Easy Pancakes with Orange-Almond Butter
instructions: Prepare the Orange-Almond Butter: Microwave 2 tablespoons butter in a medium bowl until melted, about 1 minute. Stir in orange zest, honey, almond extract, a pinch of salt, and remaining 6 tablespoons butter. Let mixture stand for 2 minutes, then whisk until smooth.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
Whisk eggs and 50g avocado oil in a second medium bowl until well combined. Whisk milk and vanilla extract into the egg mixture.
Add egg mixture to flour mixture and stir gently until just combined (batter should remain lumpy with a few streaks of flour). Let batter sit for 10 minutes before cooking.
Heat 1/2 teaspoon oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat until shimmering. Carefully wipe out oil using paper towels, leaving a thin film on bottom and sides of skillet.
Drop 1 tablespoon batter in center of skillet to test heat; if pancake is pale golden brown after 1 minute, skillet is ready. Adjust heat as needed.
Using a 1/4-cup measure, portion batter into skillet in 3 places, leaving 2 inches between portions. Gently spread batter into 4-inch rounds if necessary.
Cook until edges are set, first sides are golden brown, and bubbles on surface are just beginning to break, 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip pancakes with a thin, wide spatula and cook until second sides are golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes longer.
Repeat with remaining batter and oil as necessary. Serve warm with Orange-Almond Butter.

recipe.name: Crispy Fish Cakes with Cherry Tomato Guacamole
instructions: Flake drained mackerel and tuna into a bowl, toss with 1 tsp lemon juice, and let sit for 2 minutes.
Add cold mashed potato, lemon zest, chopped parsley, sliced spring onions, corn, peas, seasoning, and 1 beaten egg to the fish. Mix gently.
Divide mixture into 6-8 compact, flat patties.
Set up coating station: dust patties in plain flour, dip into beaten egg mixed with a splash of water, then press firmly into Panko breadcrumbs.
Place crumbed patties on a baking paper-lined tray without touching. Flash freeze for 35-45 minutes until solid. Transfer to a storage bag if keeping for later.
Cook from frozen: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium to medium-low heat. Fry patties for 6-7 minutes on the first side, flip carefully, and fry for another 5-6 minutes until golden and piping hot.
Make guacamole topping: Coarsely mash avocados with lime juice, chopped chives, salt, and pepper. Gently fold in quartered cherry tomatoes.
Top the hot, crispy fish cakes with the cool cherry tomato guacamole and serve.

recipe.name: Lemon Cheesecake
instructions: Combine Marie biscuit crumbs and melted butter, press into a 9-inch buttered tin, and refrigerate.
Dissolve lemon jelly crystals in boiling water, add lemon rind and lemon juice, and cool slightly.
Beat well-chilled evaporated milk until thick.
Beat softened cream cheese until smooth.
Blend castor sugar, vanilla, and beaten evaporated milk into the cream cheese.
Fold in the warm jelly mixture.
Pour into prepared crumb crust and chill for several hours until set.

recipe.name: Aromatic Middle Eastern Mince and Lentil Stew with Za'atar
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the mince to the pot, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, and cook until browned all over.

Stir in the ground cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, allspice, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the diced carrot, celery, zucchini, and capsicum. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to soften.

Stir in the tomato paste until well combined. Pour in the canned diced tomatoes and beef stock. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and gently simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.

Stir in the rinsed and drained lentils and half of the chopped parsley. Continue to simmer for another 5-10 minutes to let the flavours meld. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Ladle the hot stew into bowls. Sprinkle each serving generously with za'atar. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley, chopped mint, toasted pine nuts, and a dollop of plain yoghurt.

recipe.name: Shredded Chicken & Quinoa Garden Congee
instructions: Thoroughly rinse 130g rice and 30g quinoa together in a fine sieve until water runs clear to remove bitterness.
Add rinsed grains, 60g onion, 70g carrot, 80g radish, 100g mushrooms, and the white bok choy stems to the rice cooker.
Place 400g chicken thighs and 20g ginger on top. Pour in 2L stock and 7g salt (ensure it doesn't exceed the cooker's max porridge line).
Select the Congee/Porridge setting.

When done, remove chicken and shred it. Discard ginger. Stir the shredded chicken and green bok choy leaves back into the pot. Stir vigorously for 30 seconds to emulsify and create a silky texture. Let rest on 'Keep Warm' for 2 minutes to wilt the leaves.

recipe.name: Sardines on Toast
instructions: Toast the slices of wholemeal bread until golden brown.
Place the sardines on top of the toast and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Chargrilled Lemon Chicken with Garlic and Green Olive Pilaf
instructions: Read through the recipe. Pick the thyme leaves, discarding the tough stems. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Coarsely chop the olives. Juice half the lemon. Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, olives and half the thyme, stirring occasionally, for 3 mins or until the garlic is softened.

Crumble the stock cubes into the pan. Add the rice and 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Meanwhile, put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into 2 equal fillets. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 3-4 mins each side until cooked through. Transfer to a plate, reserving the pan. Drizzle the chicken with the lemon juice and cover to keep warm.

While the chicken is cooking, cut the onion into wedges. Trim the broccoli stem and thickly slice. Cut the broccoli head into small florets. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the reserved pan over high heat. Cook the onion and remaining thyme, stirring to separate the onion layers, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the onion mixture to the pilaf and stir to combine. Reserve the pan.

Put the broccoli in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Stand for 2 mins, then drain. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the reserved pan over high heat. Cook the broccoli for 2-3 mins until tender. Taste the pilaf, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the pilaf, chicken and broccoli among plates and drizzle the chicken with the resting juices to serve.

recipe.name: Greek Lentil and Spinach Soup with Lemon
instructions: In a large soup pot over medium-high heat, combine the lentils, stock or water, jalapeño, coriander, cumin, oregano and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Simmer, partially covered, until the lentils are tender, about 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes, spinach and butternut squash, re-cover and cook until the potatoes and squash are tender, another 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium heat, heat the olive oil until shimmering. Add the onion, and cook, stirring, until it starts to soften, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the celery and garlic and cook, stirring often, until they soften, 3 minutes.

Add the onion mixture to the soup, deglazing the skillet with a little bit of the broth from the soup, then add the deglazed contents back to the soup pot. Season with the salt and pepper, taste, and add more if needed. Pick out and discard the bay leaves.

Thinly slice one of the lemons and cut the other into wedges. Just before serving, stir the lemon juice into the soup. Serve the soup hot, with a lemon slice floating atop each bowl. Pass lemon wedges at the table.

recipe.name: Anti-Inflammatory Seed Crackers
instructions: Gel the base: Mix flax, chia, and 250ml water in a bowl. Let sit for 10 minutes until thick and gelatinous.
Mix flavors: Stir in the mixed seeds, nigella seeds, garlic powder, fennel seeds, salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Spread: Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Smooth the mixture evenly across the tray using a spatula. Sprinkle a touch of olive oil and salt on top.
First Bake: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the edges curl and the top feels firm.
Second Bake: Reduce heat to 165°C and bake for another 20 minutes to crisp completely.
Cool: Slide off the parchment paper onto a wire rack immediately to prevent a soggy base. Let cool completely before breaking into crackers.

recipe.name: Ultimate Keto Broccoli & Cauliflower Bake with Smoky Cheese Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
On a large baking sheet, toss the broccoli and cauliflower florets with olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread in a single layer and roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp with lightly browned edges.
Crush the pork rinds in a zip-top bag or food processor into a coarse breadcrumb texture.
In a small bowl, combine crushed pork rinds and grated Parmesan cheese, drizzle with 2 tablespoons of melted butter, and toss to coat.
Melt 3 tablespoons of unsalted butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat until brown specks form and it smells nutty.
Reduce heat to low, pour in heavy cream, and whisk to combine.
Add cubed cream cheese and whisk continuously until completely melted and smooth.
Gradually add shredded cheddar and mozzarella cheese, a handful at a time, whisking until fully melted.
Turn off heat and whisk in Dijon mustard, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a 9x13 inch baking dish, pour cheese sauce evenly over top, and stir gently to coat.
Sprinkle pork rind topping evenly over the casserole.
Bake for 10-15 minutes until bubbly around the edges and the topping is golden brown.
Let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

recipe.name: Keto Korean-Style Baked Casserole with Ham, Mushroom & Cheese
instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook, undisturbed, for 3-4 minutes until browned. Stir and continue cooking for another 2-3 minutes until moisture has evaporated.
Turn heat to medium-low. Add minced garlic and the white parts of the sliced green onions to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
In a large mixing bowl, combine shredded cabbage, diced ham, and 3/4 cup (about 84g) of the shredded cheese.
Scrape cooked mushroom, garlic, and onion mixture into the large bowl with cabbage and ham.
In a separate smaller bowl, whisk together beaten eggs, tamari, toasted sesame oil, gochugaru, almond flour, salt, and black pepper.
Pour egg batter over cabbage mixture. Add green parts of green onions (reserving 1 tbsp for garnish) and mix thoroughly until evenly combined.
Line a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper. Pour mixture into dish and spread into an even layer. Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) for conventional baking (or 180°C/350°F on combi steam mode).
Bake for 20-30 minutes until edges pull away, top is golden brown, and center is fully set.
Let rest for 5-10 minutes to set firmly before serving. Garnish with reserved green onions.

recipe.name: Chargrilled Lemon Chicken with Garlic and Green Olive Pilaf
instructions: Pick the thyme leaves, discarding the tough stems. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Coarsely chop the olives. Juice half the lemon. Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, olives and half the thyme, stirring occasionally, for 3 mins or until the garlic is softened.

Crumble the stock cubes into the pan. Add the rice and 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Meanwhile, put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into 2 equal fillets. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 3-4 mins each side until cooked through. Transfer to a plate, reserving the pan. Drizzle the chicken with the lemon juice and cover to keep warm.

While the chicken is cooking, cut the onion into wedges. Trim the broccoli stem and thickly slice. Cut the broccoli head into small florets. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the reserved pan over high heat. Cook the onion and remaining thyme, stirring to separate the onion layers, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the onion mixture to the pilaf and stir to combine. Reserve the pan.

Put the broccoli in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Stand for 2 mins, then drain. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the reserved pan over high heat. Cook the broccoli for 2-3 mins until tender. Taste the pilaf, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the pilaf, chicken and broccoli among plates and drizzle the chicken with the resting juices to serve.

recipe.name: The Ultimate Soffritto Baked Beans
instructions: Sauté the Soffritto: Heat olive oil over medium-low heat. Add onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Bloom Aromatics: Increase heat to medium. Add garlic, tomato paste, smoked paprika, oregano, and cumin. Stir constantly for 60 seconds.
Combine: Add both tins of beans, passata, and Worcestershire sauce. Season with sea salt and black pepper.
Simmer: Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10–12 minutes (or up to 30 minutes on very low with a splash of water/stock) until the sauce thickens.
Finish: Stir in the vinegar and liquid smoke just before serving. Serve over wholegrain toast.
recipe.prep_notes: Stores well in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave with a splash of water if needed.

recipe.name: HFG Teriyaki Chicken
instructions: In a small bowl, combine soy and barbecue sauces, 1/4 cup water and brown sugar. Mix well.

Spray a frying pan or wok with oil and place over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 8 minutes, until nearly cooked through and browned all over. Add broccoli and green beans to pan and stir-fry for a further 2 minutes.
Reduce heat, add soy sauce mixture to pan and toss to coat chicken and vegetables. Simmer for 1 minute, until sauce reduces slightly.
Serve over brown rice and garnish with sesame seeds and onion.

recipe.name: High-Protein Broccoli & Parmesan Soup

ingredients.name: Sea salt and cracked black pepper

instructions: Sauté the Base: Heat butter in a medium pot over medium heat. Add crushed garlic and chopped broccoli stems. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.
Steam-Boil: Pour in bone broth and bring to a rolling boil. Add broccoli florets, cover, and cook for 4–5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Temper Egg Whites: Turn off the heat. While stirring the soup in a steady circular motion, slowly stream in the liquid egg whites.
Blend: Add grated parmesan, ground mustard seed, and fresh lemon juice. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth and creamy.
Serve: Season with salt and pepper to taste.

recipe.name: The Deconstructed Cobb Bowl
instructions: Place 2 eggs in a small saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Turn off heat, cover, and let sit for 10-12 minutes. Transfer to an ice-water bath, then peel and quarter.
In a small jar or bowl, whisk together 30g extra virgin olive oil, 15g red wine vinegar, 5g Dijon mustard, 5g minced garlic, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
Place 60g bacon in a large, cold frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook until crispy and rendered, then remove to paper towels and crumble once cooled, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.

Pat 300g chicken breasts dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat 10g olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat and cook chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F). Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Melt 10g butter in the pan with the bacon fat over medium heat. Add 50g chopped yellow onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add 300g shredded cabbage with salt and pepper to the onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Divide warm cabbage base between two bowls. Arrange sliced chicken, crumbled bacon, quartered eggs, 100g halved cherry tomatoes, and 80g sliced avocado on top.
Sprinkle with 40g crumbled blue cheese and drizzle with the red wine vinaigrette.

recipe.name: Protein Fudge Brownies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg, plain Greek yogurt, and honey until well combined and smooth.
Whisk in the chocolate protein powder, unsweetened cocoa powder, oat flour, and baking powder until a thick brownie batter forms.
Gently fold in three-quarters of the dark chocolate chips, reserving the rest for topping.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared baking dish and sprinkle the remaining chocolate chips over the top.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, or until the edges are set and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with a few fudgy crumbs.
Allow the brownies to cool completely in the pan before slicing into 8 portions.
recipe.prep_notes: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze individual brownies for up to 1 month.

recipe.name: Asian-Inspired Ginger Chicken Bowl
instructions: Prep: Grate the ginger. Slice the chicken. Prep all vegetables as described. In a small jar, shake the sauce ingredients (30g tamari, 15g rice vinegar, 10g sesame oil) until combined.

Cook Chicken: Heat the 15g avocado oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned. Add the 20g of grated ginger and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the chicken is cooked through. Season with a small pinch of salt and pepper. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

Make the Warm Base: To the same pan, add the chopped bok choy stems and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Add the bok choy leaves and the 100g of baby spinach, tossing until just wilted (about 1-2 minutes). Turn off the heat and drizzle with 10g of toasted sesame oil.
Assemble: Divide the wilted greens base evenly between two bowls. Top with the ginger chicken.
Add Cold Toppings: Arrange the 60g grated carrot and 100g sliced red bell pepper alongside the chicken.
Garnish & Serve: Drizzle everything with the scratch-made tamari sauce. Garnish with the 20g sliced spring onion greens and 5g toasted sesame seeds.

recipe.name: One-Pan Chicken Shawarma Rice Bowls
instructions: In a bowl, combine the chicken with paprika, cumin, onion powder, coriander, allspice, turmeric, pepper, salt, 3 tbsp olive oil, 8 garlic cloves, half the lemon juice, and 2 tsp chicken bouillon. Mix well and marinate.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, cook chicken in batches for 6 to 8 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add butter to the same pan, then the diced yellow onions. Cook stirring often until translucent. Add garlic powder and rice spices, stirring for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the basmati rice and toast for 2 minutes while stirring. Pour in 3 cups hot water mixed with 3 tsp chicken bouillon. Stir and bring to a boil.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is fully cooked.
Mix sliced red onion, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, salt, black pepper, sumac, and half the lemon juice in a bowl for the fresh salad.
In a separate bowl, whisk mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, minced garlic, fresh parsley, salt, black pepper, remaining lemon juice, and 1 tbsp olive oil for the garlic sauce.
Serve cooked chicken over turmeric rice pilaf alongside the sumac salad and drizzled with garlic sauce.

recipe.name: Brown Stew
instructions: Trim fat from the beef steak and cut into bite-sized cubes.
Season the flour with salt and pepper, then roll the meat cubes in the seasoned flour until evenly coated.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe saucepan or casserole dish over medium-high heat and sear the meat until browned.
Add the beef stock, stirring continuously and scraping up any browned bits stuck to the base of the pan to create a smooth sauce.
Add the sliced onion, diced carrot, and diced celery. Stir well and taste for seasoning.
Transfer to the oven at 180°C. Once it starts to simmer (about 15-20 minutes), turn the heat down to 150°C and bake for about 2 hours until the beef is tender.

recipe.name: Crispy Buttermilk Chicken with Lemon Herb Rice
instructions: Combine buttermilk, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, half of the salt (2g), and hot sauce. Add chicken breasts and marinate for 4–6 hours in the refrigerator.
Place flour on one plate, beaten eggs in a bowl, and the panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, and dried herbs on a third plate.
Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess drip off. Coat each piece in flour, dip in beaten egg, and press into the breadcrumb mixture to fully coat.
Heat 55g olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook chicken for 3–4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (or bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes).
Rinse rice under cold water. In a pot, combine rice and chicken stock, bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Stir remaining 10g olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, fresh parsley, and remaining 2g salt into the cooked rice. Fluff with a fork and serve with the crispy chicken.

recipe.name: Lower-Calorie Middle Eastern Minced Beef Breakfast Hash (Kibbeh Hash - Light)

ingredients.name: Spice Mix (Cumin, Coriander, Allspice, Paprika, Chilli Flakes)

instructions: Place the bulgur in a bowl and cover with 1.4 cups of boiling water. Let sit for 10-15 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add diced onions and cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook until softened and liquid evaporates. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add extra lean minced beef, breaking it up until browned. Carefully drain off any rendered fat.
Stir in cumin, coriander, allspice, paprika, chilli flakes, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Add diced potatoes, soaked bulgur, and pine nuts to the skillet and stir well.
Pour in 3/4 cup of water, cover, and reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Cook eggs by poaching/dry frying separately, or by making wells in the hash and baking until whites are set.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and mint. Serve with light Greek yogurt, lemon wedges, and one slice of wholemeal pita per portion.

recipe.name: The Clean High-Protein Keto Breakfast Traybake
instructions: Preheat your fan-forced oven to 180°C. Line a large, rimmed baking tray with baking paper to ensure easy cleanup and prevent the eggs from sticking.

In a small bowl, combine the raw beef mince with the rubbed sage, dried thyme, ground white pepper, fine sea salt, and a pinch of nutmeg. Use your hands to work the spices thoroughly into the meat so the flavor is evenly distributed.

Place the cubed pork loin on one section of the tray. Next to it, break the seasoned beef mince into small, bite-sized rustic crumbles (about the size of marbles). Arrange the thick portobello mushroom slices, king oyster mushrooms, and whole cherry tomatoes on the remaining space.

Drizzle the 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil evenly across the pork cubes, beef crumbles, mushrooms, and tomatoes. Give the whole tray a final light sprinkle of sea salt and cracked black pepper.

Pop the tray onto the middle rack of the oven and bake for 15 minutes. The pork will cook through, the seasoned beef crumbles will crisp up on the edges, the mushrooms will soften, and the cherry tomatoes will begin to blister beautifully.

Carefully slide the tray out of the oven. Scatter the fresh baby spinach over the hot tray—it will begin to wilt instantly from the heat. Use a spatula to clear two small pockets on the baking paper, then crack the two free-range eggs directly into them.

Return the tray to the oven for a final 5 minutes. Remove once the egg whites are completely set and opaque, but the yolks are still soft. Serve immediately, using the runny yolks as a rich, whole-food dipping sauce for your roasted meats and mushrooms.

recipe.name: The Fast-Braise Chicken Cacciatore
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F). Season the whole thigh fillets generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven over high heat until shimmering. Sear the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side just to get a deep, dark brown color on the surface. (They will still be raw in the middle). Remove to a plate.

Drop the heat to medium. Add the onions, peppers, and mushrooms to the remaining oil/chicken juices. Cook for 5–6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine, using a wooden spoon to aggressively scrape up all the savory brown bits stuck to the pan. Let it bubble for 2 minutes until reduced by half.

In a cup, sprinkle the gelatin over the chicken stock and let it sit for 2 minutes to bloom. Pour the stock/gelatin mix, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, fish sauce, olives, and herbs into the pan. Stir well and bring to a simmer.

Tuck the chicken fillets and any resting juices completely into the liquid so they are fully submerged. Put the lid on the pot completely closed and place it in the oven for 15 minutes to lock in moisture. Remove the lid completely and cook for another 5–10 minutes to allow the oven's dry heat to concentrate and thicken the sauce.
Discard the woody herb stems. The sauce should be velvet-thick and clinging to the meat. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil.

recipe.name: Jewish Apple Cake

ingredients.name: Neutral vegetable oil (such as avocado oil)

instructions: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350 degrees. Coat a large (10- to 15-cup) Bundt pan with baking spray, or grease thoroughly with a thin layer of oil, paying extra attention to the center tube.
In a small bowl, whisk together 5 tablespoons (60 grams) of the granulated sugar and the cinnamon.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt.

In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, or using a large bowl and a handheld mixer, beat the remaining 2 cups (400 grams) of granulated sugar, the eggs and oil on medium speed until thoroughly combined, creamy, slightly aerated and lighter in color, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the vanilla and mix on medium until incorporated. Using about a third of each, mix in the flour mixture and orange juice in three alternating additions on low, beating well after each.

Pour half the batter into the prepared pan and smooth it into an even layer. Place half of the sliced apples in a ring around the batter in a fan pattern. Sprinkle half the sugar and cinnamon mixture over the apples. Pour on the remaining batter, level it and repeat the layering with the rest of the apples and sugar mixture.
Bake for 60 to 65 minutes, or until a cake tester inserted into the center comes out clean.

Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let rest for 10 minutes. Use a small flexible spatula or round-edged knife to loosen the sides of the cake from the pan and turn onto the rack. Let cool completely, then dust with confectioners’ sugar before serving.
recipe.prep_notes: The baked cake can be covered and stored at room temperature for up to 5 days, or individual slices can be wrapped and frozen for several months.

recipe.name: Keto Greek Chicken & Salad
instructions: Combine 2 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, 1 tsp dried oregano, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl to create the marinade.
Add chicken thighs to the marinade and let sit for 30 minutes to 4 hours.
Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 4-6 minutes per side until crispy and cooked through. If necessary, finish in a 160°C (320°F) oven for 10 minutes.
Remove chicken from heat, allow to rest for a few minutes, then slice.
Chop tomato and cucumber. Combine in a bowl with pickled red onion, Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese.
Whisk together 2 Tbsp olive oil, red wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss salad ingredients with the vinaigrette.
Divide the salad into portions and top with the sliced chicken.

recipe.name: Aromatic Mughlai Beef & Lentil Curry (Oven Method)
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (140°C fan-forced) with rack in the lower-middle position.
Heat a heavy oven-safe Dutch oven over high heat with a touch of ghee. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned; set aside.
Drop heat to medium, add remaining ghee, and sauté onion, garlic, ginger, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garam masala, cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Stir constantly for 60 seconds to bloom in the fat.
Return beef and juices to the pot. Add rinsed lentils and bone broth. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Place a sheet of baking paper or foil over the pot, seal tightly with the lid, and transfer to the oven for 2 hours.
Remove lid. Simmer uncovered on the stove for 3-5 minutes if needed to thicken. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.

recipe.name: Serious Eats Foolproof Pan Pizza
instructions: Combine flour, salt, yeast, water, and 8g oil into a sticky dough. Cover and rest at room temperature for 8 to 24 hours.
Put 1 to 2 tbsp olive oil into two 10-inch cast iron skillets. Divide dough in half, shape into balls, and place one in each pan, coating in oil.
Cover and let rest for 2 hours. Preheat oven to 290°C during the final hour.
Press dough with fingertips to fill the bottom of the pans to the edges.
Spread sauce and mozzarella all the way to the absolute edge so the cheese touches the pan wall.
Bake at 290°C for 12–15 minutes until bubbly and dark golden.
If the bottom needs more crisping, place the skillet on the stovetop over medium heat for 1–3 minutes.

recipe.name: Low-FODMAP Chicken Shawarma with Tahini Sauce
instructions: Make the Marinade: In a large bowl, whisk together the lactose-free yogurt, olive oil, 1/4 cup garlic-infused olive oil, 1/4 cup lemon juice, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, turmeric, allspice, pepper, and 2 tsp salt.
Marinate the Chicken: Add the chicken thighs to the bowl and mix until every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight.
Preheat your oven's broiler to its highest setting. Move an oven rack to the second-highest position.
Arrange the marinated chicken thighs in a single layer on a foil-lined baking sheet.
Broil for 10-15 minutes per side, until the edges are charred and the chicken is cooked through.
Move the cooked chicken to a cutting board and let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice into thin, long shaved strips.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat. Add the sliced chicken to the hot pan (in batches if needed) and sear for 2-3 minutes, tossing, until the edges get extra crispy.
Make the Tahini Sauce: In a medium bowl, add the tahini, 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1 tsp garlic-infused olive oil, and 1/2 tsp salt.
Begin to whisk until thick, then add lukewarm water 1 tablespoon at a time, whisking continuously until smooth and drizzly.

recipe.name: Middle Eastern Lamb Bowl with Tahini Sauce
instructions: Prep all the cold salad ingredients (cucumber, tomato, parsley, mint) and mix them in a bowl. Set aside. In a separate small bowl, combine the dried herbs for the lamb (oregano, sumac, dried mint).

In a third bowl, whisk the tahini and lemon juice together. Add the cold water, 1 tbsp at a time, whisking vigorously until it becomes a smooth, creamy, pourable sauce. Add a pinch of salt and set aside.

Pat the diced lamb very dry. Heat the extra virgin olive oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the lamb in a single layer and sear for 2-3 minutes until well-browned. Add the dried herb mix, salt, and pepper, and toss for 30 seconds until fragrant. Remove lamb from the pan.
To the same pan, add the garlic-infused olive oil and shredded cabbage. Sauté over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, scraping up any bits from the lamb, until the cabbage is tender-crisp.
Divide the warm cabbage base evenly between two bowls. Top with the seared lamb and a large scoop of the cold cucumber-herb salad mix.
Drizzle generously with the tahini sauce and sprinkle with toasted chopped walnuts before serving.

recipe.name: Ridiculously Good Air Fryer Chicken Breast
instructions: Cut each chicken breast into thin, flat pieces (3-4 thin pieces per breast). Pat dry if moisture is present.
Mix spices, salt, brown sugar, and cornstarch together. Sprinkle over the chicken pieces in a bowl. Add avocado oil and toss to coat thoroughly.
Preheat the air fryer.
Place the chicken in an even layer on the air fryer basket/grate, leaving space for air to circulate.
Air fry at 415°F (212°C) for 10 minutes (up to 13 minutes for larger pieces) until internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest for a moment before slicing and serving.

recipe.name: Spiced Chickpea & Green Base
instructions: Blend the green chili, frozen peas, frozen spinach, coriander, fish stock, and fish sauce until combined but still slightly textured.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and temper the ginger, brown mustard seeds, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add the red chili flakes and pour in the blended green mixture.
Simmer for 8–10 minutes to reduce the liquid.
Stir in the drained chickpeas until warmed through.
recipe.prep_notes: Divide base into freezer molds once cooled. Reheat from frozen and gently simmer thin white fish fillets in the sauce until cooked through.

recipe.name: Slow-Cooked Beef & (Tinned) Lentil Ragu

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (Shiraz or Cabernet Sauvignon)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Pat the chuck roast dry with paper towels and season generously on all sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the beef for 3-4 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms all over, then remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes. Pour in the red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, and let simmer until reduced by half.
Return seared beef and any resting juices to the pot. Add canned tomatoes, beef stock, bay leaves, and dried herbs. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover with lid and transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Cook for 3.5 to 4 hours, until the beef is completely fall-apart tender.
Remove pot from oven, place on stovetop over low heat, and discard bay leaves.
Shred the beef directly in the pot using two forks and stir into the sauce.
Gently fold in the rinsed and drained tinned lentils. Simmer gently on the stovetop for 5-10 minutes to heat through.
Turn off heat, season to taste with salt and pepper, stir in balsamic vinegar if desired, and serve garnished with chopped fresh herbs.

recipe.name: Mediterranean Lemon & Herb Chicken Power Bowl
instructions: In a medium saucepan, bring the 500g of chicken broth to a boil. Add the 240g of brown rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 25-30 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

About 5 minutes before the rice is done, bring a separate pot of water to a boil. Add the 300g of broccoli florets and cook for 2 minutes until bright green. Add the 200g of frozen peas and cook for another minute. Drain immediately and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process.
In a small bowl, whisk together the 40g of olive oil, 60g of lemon juice, 10g of minced garlic, and 4g of dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked rice, blanched broccoli and peas, and the 600g of shredded chicken. Pour the dressing over the top and toss everything together until well-coated.
Divide the mixture evenly among four bowls or airtight containers. Top each serving with 10g of toasted almonds before serving.

recipe.name: The "Cheater's" All-American Beef Stew
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). Season the beef chuck roast steaks heavily with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear steaks until dark brown on both sides, then transfer to a plate.
Lower heat to medium. Add onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Stir for 5 minutes until starting to soften and brown slightly.
Add garlic and stir for 1 minute. Pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to the bottom, and simmer for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Meanwhile, combine stock, unflavored gelatin, soy sauce, fish sauce, and tomato paste in a jug, allowing gelatin to bloom for 5 minutes.
Cut seared beef steaks into 1.5-inch cubes and toss with flour in a bowl.
Return beef and accumulated juices to the pot. Pour in stock mixture, add bay leaves and thyme sprig, and stir well.
Bring pot to a simmer on stove. Cover with lid slightly ajar and braise in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is tender.
Remove from oven, skim off excess fat if desired, stir in frozen peas, and let warm through for 2 minutes before serving.

recipe.name: The "Blank Canvas" Braised Beef
instructions: Pat the roast dry and season generously with salt. Sear it on all sides in hot oil in a Dutch oven until deeply browned.
Remove the beef. Add the quartered onions and smashed garlic to the pot and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the bay leaves, peppercorns, and enough stock or water to come halfway up the meat. Bring to a simmer on the stove.
Cover the pot and place it in a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Cook for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until the meat is completely tender and falling apart.

Let the beef cool slightly in its liquid. Shred the meat with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat and the bay leaves. Store the shredded beef in its own cooking liquid in an airtight container in the fridge.
recipe.prep_notes: Store the shredded beef in its cooking liquid in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze in portions.

recipe.name: Lower-Calorie Sardine Pâté
instructions: Open the can of sardines and drain the water thoroughly. Place the sardines in a bowl and remove any large spines if desired.
Add the cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, red onion, and garlic to the bowl with the sardines.
Using a fork, potato masher, or immersion blender, mash and combine the ingredients until you achieve your desired consistency.
Season with freshly ground black pepper to taste, adjust lemon juice or mustard if needed, and fold in the fresh herbs.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes for a firmer pâté.
Serve with cucumber slices, celery sticks, bell pepper strips, or thin slices of whole-grain toast.
recipe.prep_notes: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipe.name: Fast Pork Dumplings
instructions: Finely grate the zest of half the lime, then juice the lime. Combine the lime zest, lime juice, aioli, sesame oil, sesame seeds, 3 tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp sugar in a bowl.
Thinly slice the celery and spring onion on an angle.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a medium frypan over high heat. Stir-fry the celery, spring onion and vegetable mix for 5 mins or until just tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, heat a generous drizzle of oil in a separate medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the dumplings, without turning, for 2-3 mins until golden on one side.

Carefully add 60ml (¼ cup) water to the dumplings (take extra care adding water to the hot pan as the oil can spit and the steam created is very hot). Cover and steam for 3 mins or until the dumplings are tender.
Divide the vegetables and dumplings among bowls. Drizzle with the dressing and scatter with a pinch of shichimi togarashi to serve.

recipe.name: Easy Asian Barbecue Chicken with Udon Noodles and Rainbow Veggies
instructions: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the noodles. Thinly slice the cabbage. Halve the carrot lengthwise and thinly slice. Thinly slice the spring onion, keeping the white and green parts separate.

Combine the cornflour and Chinese barbecue seasoning in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Dust the chicken with the cornflour mixture and shake off the excess. Heat 1 tbs oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5-6 mins each side until cooked through. Remove from the pan, reserving the pan. (Wipe the pan clean if there are burnt pieces.)
While the chicken is cooking, combine the kecap manis, 1 tbs white vinegar, 1 tbs soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar in a bowl.
Cook the noodles in the pan of boiling water for 8 mins or until tender. Drain, then rinse under cold water to prevent the noodles from sticking.
Heat 1 tbs oil in the reserved pan over high heat. Stir-fry the cabbage and carrot for 3 mins or until just tender. Add the white part of the spring onion and stir-fry for 1 min.

Add the noodles, sauce and spinach to the vegetables and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until heated through. Remove from the heat. Slice the chicken. Divide the noodle stir-fry and chicken among bowls. Scatter with the remaining spring onion to serve.

recipe.name: Spiced Lamb and Couscous with Mint-Cucumber Yoghurt
instructions: Crush or finely chop the garlic. Finely chop the onion, carrot and tomato. Coarsely grate the cucumber, then put in a sieve over a bowl to drain until required (discard any liquid). Pick half the coriander leaves. Finely chop the remaining coriander, keeping the leaves and stems separate. Finely chop the mint leaves, discarding the stems.

Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, onion and carrot, stirring regularly, for 4-5 mins until the carrot is slightly softened. Add the lamb mince and Moroccan seasoning and cook, breaking up the lumps with a spoon, for 5 mins or until well browned.

Meanwhile, crumble 1 stock cube into a heatproof jug, add 200ml boiling water and stir to dissolve. Put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl, add 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil, pour over the stock and cover with a plate. Stand for 5 mins or until the stock is absorbed.

Stir the tomato and chopped coriander into the mince mixture. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook, stirring, for a further 5 mins or until the tomato is softened. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, then add half the cucumber and half the mint and stir to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Combine the yoghurt, remaining cucumber and remaining mint in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Divide the couscous and lamb mixture among plates. Spoon over the mint-cucumber yoghurt and scatter with the coriander leaves to serve.

recipe.name: Spicy Chicken Rendang Curry
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

While the rice is cooking, crush or finely chop the garlic. Coarsely chop the tomato. Coarsely chop the cucumber. Crumble 1 stock cube into a heatproof jug, add 125ml boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Thinly slice the chicken into strips. Heat 1 tbs oil in a medium deep frypan over high heat. Cook the chicken, stirring, for 2 mins or until browned (the chicken won't be cooked through). Remove from the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium-high. Cook the garlic and curry paste, stirring, for 1-2 mins until fragrant and the curry paste splits. Stir in the stock and coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 mins to develop the flavour.

Add the chicken and peas to the curry sauce and return to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring, for 2 mins or until tender and the sauce is slightly thickened. Stir in 2 tsp white vinegar. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Put the tomato, cucumber and 2 tsp white vinegar in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Fluff the rice with a fork. Divide the rice and curry among bowls. Scatter with the fried shallots and serve with the salsa.

recipe.name: Low-Cal Greek-Style Chicken
instructions: Halve the carrot and zucchini lengthwise, then slice on an angle. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Finely grate the zest of half the lemon, then juice the half. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges. Drain and rinse the beans. Pick the dill sprigs, discarding the stems.

Put half the mint and garlic seasoning and 2 tsp olive oil in a large bowl. Put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into fillets. Add the chicken to the seasoned oil and turn to coat.
Heat a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, turning regularly, for 4-8 mins until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs olive oil in a large frypan over medium-high heat. Add the carrot, garlic and lemon zest and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-6 mins until the carrot is slightly softened. Add the zucchini and beans and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until heated through.

Add the spinach, remaining mint and garlic seasoning and 1 tbs water to the bean mixture, cover and cook for 2 mins or until the spinach is just wilted. Remove the pan from the heat. Add half the dill and 2 tsp lemon juice, season with pepper and stir well to combine.

Slice the chicken. Divide the chicken and bean mixture among plates. Crumble over the feta, scatter with the remaining dill and drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil, if desired. Serve with the lemon wedges.

recipe.name: Easy Beef and Sweet Soy Stir-Fry
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 minutes.
Halve the carrot and zucchini lengthwise and thinly slice on an angle. Crush or finely chop the garlic.
Combine the oyster sauce, half the kecap manis (20g), 2 tbsp water, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp sugar in a bowl.

Separate the beef stir-fry. Dust the beef with half the cornflour (10g) and shake off any excess. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large deep frypan over high heat until hot. Stir-fry the beef for 1-2 minutes until browned. Remove from the pan.
Heat 2 tsp oil in the same pan over high heat. Stir-fry the carrot for 1 minute or until starting to soften. Add the zucchini and stir-fry for a further 2-3 minutes until just tender.

Add the garlic, sauce, cashews, spinach, beef, and any resting juices to the vegetables. Cook, stirring, for a further 1-2 minutes until the spinach is wilted and the sauce is slightly thickened. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve with the stir-fry.

recipe.name: Beef Rump Steak Bowl - 15-Min Cheesy
instructions: Thinly slice the onion. Coarsely chop the capsicum. Coarsely grate half the cheese. Put the steaks and half the teriyaki sauce in a bowl and turn to coat. Season with pepper.

Heat a medium frypan over high heat until hot. Reduce the heat to medium-high and cook the steaks, turning regularly, for 4-6 mins for medium-rare, or until cooked to your liking. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.

While the steaks are resting, heat a drizzle of olive oil in the same pan over high heat. Cook the onion and capsicum, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 mins until lightly charred. Massage the packet of rice to loosen and add to the vegetables. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 mins until heated through.

Put the steaks on top of the rice mixture and scatter over the cheese. Cook, covered, for 1-2 mins until the cheese is melted. Combine the kaleslaw mix, aioli and 2 tsp red wine vinegar in a large bowl. Slice the steaks. Divide the rice mixture, kaleslaw and steak among bowls to serve.

recipe.name: Hoisin-Glazed Chicken and Coconut Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put the rice, 100ml coconut milk and 200ml water in a small saucepan, season with salt and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the liquid is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.
Meanwhile, trim the beans and cut to 1.5cm lengths. Halve the carrot lengthwise, then thinly slice on an angle. Finely grate the zest of half the lime, then cut the half into wedges.
Combine the hoisin sauce and Chinese barbecue seasoning in a large bowl. Thinly slice the chicken into strips. Add the chicken to the hoisin sauce mixture and stir to coat.
Heat 2 tsp oil in a medium deep frypan over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 4 mins or until cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and cover to keep warm.

Heat 2 tsp oil in the same pan over high heat. Stir-fry the beans and carrot for 3-4 mins until just tender. Add 2 tbs water and cook, scraping the base to incorporate the flavour. Remove the pan from the heat.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the cucumber on an angle and season lightly with salt. Fluff the rice with a fork, add the lime zest and stir to combine. Divide the rice, chicken and stir-fried vegetables among plates. Serve with the cucumber and lime wedges.

recipe.name: Low-Carb Spicy Mexican Chicken
instructions: Crush or finely chop the garlic. Coarsely chop the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Thinly slice the cabbage with a sharp knife or mandoline. Shred the zucchini using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Halve the cucumber lengthwise, scrape out the seeds using a teaspoon, then thinly slice.

Put the garlic, 1½ tsp Mexican spice blend, 1 tbs olive oil and 1 tsp honey in a shallow dish, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into fillets. Add the chicken to the marinade and turn to coat.

Cook the pepitas in a cold medium frypan over medium heat, tossing, for 3-4 mins until toasted. Remove from the pan. Increase the heat to medium-high. Cook the chicken, turning regularly, for 4-8 mins until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.
Meanwhile, combine the aioli, half the coriander, ½ tsp Mexican spice blend, 2 tsp white wine vinegar and 2 tsp water in a large bowl.
Add the cabbage, zucchini, cucumber, pepitas and remaining coriander to the dressing and gently toss to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Slice the chicken. Divide the slaw and chicken among plates. Drizzle the chicken with any resting juices to serve.

recipe.name: Seared Tex-Mex Chicken with Cheesy Sweet Potato and Tomato Salsa
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line a large oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potatoes into 1cm-thick slices. Crush or finely chop the garlic.

Put the sweet potato on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, scatter with the garlic and ½ tsp Tex-Mex seasoning and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, then roast for 20 mins or until golden and tender.

Meanwhile, finely chop the tomato. Finely chop the coriander, discarding the stems. Combine the tomato, coriander, 2 tsp extra virgin olive oil and 1 tsp white wine vinegar in a bowl. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into fillets. Put the chicken in a shallow dish, scatter with the remaining Tex-Mex seasoning, drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and turn to coat.
Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 2-4 mins each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.

Finely grate the parmesan, then scatter over the roasted sweet potato. Roast for a further 5 mins or until the parmesan is melted and golden. Put the spinach and 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Divide the sweet potato, spinach and chicken among plates. Serve with the tomato salsa.

recipe.name: Low-Carb Chicken and Avocado Salad
instructions: Check your avocado is ripe before starting this recipe. Shred the carrot using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Thinly slice the radish. Thinly slice the spring onion. Slice the avocado.

Put 1 tsp dried mint and 2 tsp olive oil in a large bowl, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Put the chicken flat on a board, put your hand on top and halve horizontally into fillets. Add the chicken to the seasoned oil and turn to coat.
Put the sunflower seeds in a cold medium frypan over medium heat. Toast, tossing, for 2-3 mins until evenly golden. Remove from the pan.
Heat the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 2-4 mins each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.

Meanwhile, juice the lime. Put 1 tbs lime juice, 1 tsp dried mint, 1 tbs extra virgin olive oil, ½ tsp wholegrain mustard and ½ tsp honey in a large bowl, season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine.
Slice the chicken. Add the carrot, radish, onion, avocado and spinach to the dressing and gently toss to combine. Divide the salad and chicken among bowls. Scatter with the sunflower seeds to serve.

recipe.name: Low-Cal Caribbean Steak with Sweet Potato Mash and Veggies
instructions: Crush or finely chop the garlic. Discard the husk and silks from the corn, then slice the kernels from the cob. Thinly slice the silverbeet. Finely chop the tomato. Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 3cm chunks.

Put the sweet potato in a medium saucepan, cover with cold salted water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 12-14 mins until tender. Drain, return to the pan and cover to keep warm.
Meanwhile, put ½ tsp Caribbean seasoning and 2 tsp olive oil in a shallow dish, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Add the steaks and turn to coat.

Heat a medium deep frypan over high heat until hot. Reduce the heat to medium-high and cook the steaks for 2-3 mins each side for medium-rare, or until cooked to your liking. Remove from the pan and rest for 3 mins.

While the steaks are resting, heat 2 tsp olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic, corn and silverbeet, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Stir in the tomato and ½ tsp red wine vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat.

Mash the sweet potato until smooth. Stir in remaining Caribbean seasoning and 2 tsp olive oil. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Cut the lime into wedges. Slice the steaks against the grain. Divide mash, vegetables and steak among plates and drizzle the steak with any resting juices. Serve with lime wedges.

recipe.name: Easy One-Pan Mediterranean Chicken
instructions: Thinly slice the onion. Cut the capsicum into 1cm-thick strips. Quarter the unpeeled potatoes. Thinly slice the silverbeet stems, then coarsely chop the leaves, keeping the stems and leaves separate.
Cut the chicken into 4cm chunks and season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Add the onion, capsicum and chicken and cook, stirring, for 4-5 mins until the chicken is browned.

Add the tomatoes, potato, silverbeet stems, 1½ tsp Italian seasoning, ½ tsp sugar and 80ml (⅓ cup) water to the chicken mixture and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 mins or until the potato is almost tender.
Stir the silverbeet leaves into the chicken mixture. Cook, covered, for 5-6 mins until the potato and silverbeet are tender and the sauce is thickened.
Stir the olives and capers into the chicken and vegetable mixture. Remove from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the chicken and vegetables among plates to serve.

recipe.name: Ginger Beef and Broccoli

ingredients.name: Beef rump steak, trimmed of fat and cut into strips

instructions: Heat oil in a frypan and brown the beef over a medium high heat - it doesn’t need to be cooked all the way through. Remove from pan.
Turn down the temperature and into the pan, add ginger, tamari, sweet chilli and water - stir to make a sauce.
Add the broccoli and cook through for 4-5 minutes, stirring regularly. Put a lid on between stirring to help steam the broccoli.
Add beef back into the pan and stir to coat in the sauce.
Serve topped with the spring onion.

recipe.name: Beef Bolognese
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and saute onions and mushrooms for 5 minutes, until onion is translucent and soft.
Add beef mince and fry off for 4-5 minutes until browned.
Add the tinned tomatoes, tomato paste, stock and oregano - stir through and simmer for 5-10 minutes, stirring regularly. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Arrange raw spiralised zucchini on your plate, top with bolognese and parmesan.
recipe.prep_notes: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Defrost and reheat before serving.

recipe.name: Meatloaf
instructions: Preheat oven to fan forced 180º C/200º C/350º F/Gas mark 4 and line an appropriate sized loaf tin with baking paper.
In a small bowl mix together the tomato paste and half the oregano for the topping. Set aside.
In a larger bowl, combine remaining ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer mixture into loaf tin.
Smooth over the tomato paste topping and bake for 25 mins.
Remove loaf from oven and rest for at least 10 minutes to allow juices to reabsorb before slicing with a serrated bread knife and serving.
recipe.prep_notes: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Batch cook and freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Defrost and reheat before serving.

recipe.name: Tuna and Chickpea Salad
instructions: Drain the tuna and reserve the oil. Put the tuna into a large bowl and break it into flakes with a fork.
Add the chickpeas, red onion, red capsicum and parsley to the bowl and mix.
Whisk together the lemon juice and reserved tuna oil to create a dressing. Season well.
Pour the dressing over your salad mix, add the spinach leaves and lightly toss everything together. Serve immediately and enjoy!

recipe.name: Peanut Butter Oat Smoothie
instructions: Add all ingredients to a blender and blitz for 60 seconds.
Pour the smoothie into a glass and add ice-cubes. Serve immediately or place in the refrigerator until ready to drink.

recipe.name: Italian Lentil Salad
instructions: Whisk together the olive oil and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Place all the ingredients for the salad into a bowl with the lentils, pour over the lemon dressing and toss together to serve.

recipe.name: Turkey Chilli with Broccoli
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion and garlic for 4-5 minutes, until soft.
Add the turkey mince and cook, stirring frequently, until browned.
Stir in the chilli flakes, chopped tomatoes and kidney beans and pour over water. Season well.
Bring to the boil and then simmer for 20-25 minutes, adding a little more water if necessary.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli until tender.
Serve the chilli with the broccoli.

recipe.name: Chicken Curry
instructions: In a frying pan over low-medium heat, dry-fry the ground coriander, cumin, and turmeric until fragrant. Add a dash of water and cook into a paste.
Turn the heat to medium, add the olive oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger in the spices for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and brown it all over, cooking for approximately 5 minutes. Add in the capsicum and cook for a further 2 minutes.

Add the vegetable stock and tomato paste along with the chilli. Bring to a fast simmer and cook for 15 minutes with the lid off, or until chicken is cooked through. Season to taste with sea salt and black pepper.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted. Serve topped with Greek yogurt and fresh coriander.

recipe.name: Greek Salad
instructions: Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, lettuce, cucumber, red capsicum, and red onion to a large bowl. Crumble in the goats cheese and toss.
In a small bowl or jar, mix the vinegar, olive oil, basil and oregano. Season to taste.
Pour the dressing evenly over the salad and enjoy!
recipe.prep_notes: Store dressing and salad leftovers separately in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Mix and serve.

recipe.name: Blueberry Yogurt with Nuts and Seeds
instructions: Blend or mix yogurt and berries together.
Serve topped with mixed nuts and seeds. Enjoy!

recipe.name: Green Breakfast Smoothie
instructions: Place all of the ingredients into a blender and blend until you have reached a texture that you are happy with.
Pour the smoothie into a glass, add ice cubes and enjoy!
recipe.prep_notes: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipe.name: Apple Pear and Hazelnut Yogurt
instructions: Place the pear and hazelnuts into a food processor and pulse a few times to form a rough paste.
Place the paste at the bottom of a dish, add the yogurt and mix in the chunks of apple.

recipe.name: Pizza Courgette
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F/Gas mark 6.
Brush the open side of the courgette with oil and place open face up on a lined baking tray - bake for 20 minutes.
Mix the oregano and chilli flakes with the tomato paste.
When courgette has had about 20 minutes in the oven, remove and spread the tomato mix over the open halves, topping with olives and cheeses.
Return to the oven for 10-15 minutes until the cheese is starting to golden.
Serve immediately.

recipe.name: Pumpkin and Pancetta Soup
instructions: Heat a saucepan over medium heat. Add the olive oil, onion, garlic and pancetta. Cook until the onion starts to soften, approx. 5 minutes.
Add the stock, pumpkin, tomatoes and the lentils and bring to the boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, or until pumpkin is tender, stirring occasionally.
Add the broccoli and simmer for an additional 5 minutes. You may choose to blitz soup with a hand blender until smooth or leave chunky.
Serve in a warm bowl, season with sea salt and black pepper, and top with parsley.

recipe.name: Cottage Cheese Cucumber and Salmon Salad
instructions: Slice cucumber lengthways and chop into small cubes and put into a medium sized bowl.
Add the cottage cheese, dill, spring onion and lemon juice then mix well to combine.
On a small plate, serve the cottage cheese mixture and season with sea salt and black pepper. Add the smoked salmon to the top of the salad.
recipe.prep_notes: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Serve cold.

recipe.name: Lentil Spinach Dhal
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a low heat. Add onion and cook for 4-5 minutes, or until the onion is soft. Add the chilli, cumin and turmeric and cook for a further 2 minutes, stirring.

Add the lentils to the pan and turn up the heat. Fry the lentils for a few minutes and then pour in the vegetable stock. Turn the heat down and leave the lentils to simmer for approximately 15 minutes, or until the lentils are swollen and the stock has been absorbed, stir occasionally.
